summary: SCCM policy decryption failure blocks device provisioning after SSD replacement
description:
Issue summary:
After a standard depot SSD replacement, devices fail to complete provisioning: the SCCM client reports policy decryption errors and the provisioning agent enters a retry loop. This appears correlated with repaired devices that had encrypted SCCM client keys prior to SSD swap.

Impact:
- Multiple recent depot repairs (3 devices reported so far) cannot reach 'Enrollment Complete' state and are stuck in provisioning for >2 hours.
- Devices cannot pull corporate policies or enroll into Intune co-management until SCCM client recovers.
- Affects engineers receiving repaired laptops; blocking productivity and delaying asset returns to inventory.

Environment:
- Production repair pipeline (depot) in us-west region.
- Model: Dell Latitude 7440 with BitLocker enabled and SCCM client configured for certificate-based client auth.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioning agent logs show repeated failures decrypting policy blob (error: "policy_decrypt_failure: 0x80090016").
- SCCM client shows "MP certificate thumbprint mismatch" and reports unable to validate policy signature.
- Machine attempts self-recover (client re-register) and eventually falls back to manual remediation after repeated retries.

Expected behavior:
- After SSD replacement and OS restore from depot image, SCCM client should re-enroll automatically or fall back to a clear re-registration flow that doesn’t require manual cert recovery.

Candidate root cause:
- During depot repair, the imaging process preserves the device identity GUID but the TPM-bound SCCM client cert/key is lost or replaced by the repair image. The server-side policy is still encrypted for the original key, causing decryption failure.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual local admin intervention: stop SCCM client service, delete CCM client certificate store entries, trigger client re-registration with provisioning script (reimage-scripts/tools/force-sccm-regen.sh). This recovers ~80% of devices but requires tech time.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Take a device with existing SCCM enrollment and BitLocker enabled.
2) Replace SSD and re-apply depot image used for repairs (current depot image: depot-image-2025-11).
3) Boot device and allow provisioning agent to run automatically.
4) Observe SCCM client logs under C:\Windows\CCM\Logs (PolicyAgent.log, ClientIDManagerStartup.log) for decrypt/MP cert errors.
5) Watch provisioning agent status in console — device never reaches 'Enrollment Complete' and retries decrypt step.
logs: PolicyAgent.log -- 2026-03-10 08:21:13 -- ERROR policy_decrypt_failure: 0x80090016 -- attempted policy id=0x4f3b
ClientIDManagerStartup.log -- 2026-03-10 08:21:14 -- WARNING MP certificate thumbprint mismatch: local thumbprint=ab12... vs server=cd34...
comments: 2026-03-11 - Jordan Meyers: Reported by depot techs after 3 repaired units failed to finish provisioning. Attached client logs from first affected device.
2026-03-11 - Ravi Kapoor: Assigned to investigate. Initial hypothesis is certificate/TMP key inconsistency after SSD change. Will validate whether imaging process retains TPM-bound key references.

2026-03-12 - Elena Ortiz (Depot Lead): Confirmed depot image used is the standard repair image (depot-image-2025-11). Depot does not currently run a post-image SCCM client rekey step unless manually requested.

2026-03-12 - Ravi Kapoor: Reproduced on test bench following steps. Confirmed error 0x80090016 and certificate thumbprint mismatch. Escalating to ConfigMgmt eng for policy-side guidance. Filed PR to add rekey step to repair playbook (see related_github_prs).
investigation_notes: Checked SCCM server logs for policy encryption mapping — server still targets original client key (client-id GUID matches), but certificate thumbprint changed after image restore.
Validated TPM PCRs on repaired device (no irregularities) — likely imaging process overwrote local client certs without updating server mapping.
Tested force-sccm-regen.sh which deletes CCM certs and triggers new client key generation; devices recover and policies decrypt normally after server sees new thumbprint.
ConfigMgmt team notes: certificate rotation/validation expects a client-side hook post-image; depot images are currently optimized for quick imaging and skip certificate re-provision step.
resolution: In Progress - temporary manual remediation documented and used for affected units (force-sccm-regen.sh). Next steps: (1) Update depot repair playbook to run SCCM client rekey script post-image, (2) Add an automated safety check in provisioning agent to detect policy_decrypt_failure and trigger guided re-registration flow, (3) Coordinate with ConfigMgmt to add server-side fallback when thumbprint mismatch is detected.
next_steps: PR to depot image playbook to add rekey step (owner: PlatformOps) - target deploy 2026-03-18
Create provisioning-agent ticket to add recoverable path on policy_decrypt_failure (owner: Provisioning Eng) - target triage 2026-03-15
Notify depot technicians and update repair SOP with manual rekey instructions until playbook change lands
